summary: Adds a permanent end-to-end regression guard proving the MCP raw `args` field cannot inject blocked flags (--deliver/--config) into CLI argv; the review's claimed bypass is a verified false positive.
reason: Greptile PR #1528 P1 security claimed raw args bypass the blocked-flag boundary. Reproduced end-to-end through shellOutToCLI: validatePositionalArgsForMCPAtOffset already rejects flag-prefixed tokens on the SplitShellArgs path ('flag-like' error), and the single-positional path passes the whole string as ONE exec arg cobra never re-parses as a flag. No code change to the generated boundary; test-only file so the guarantee is locked against future regen drift.
validated_outcome: Both regression tests pass: zero/multi-positional flag tokens are rejected with the flag-like error; single-positional embedded flags never appear as a distinct argv token.
